answer: Each agent’s influence can be capped until it posts a bond that is slashed if independent peers verify a double-spend or fabricated work claim. To make many fake identities count, an attacker must lock capital behind each one and risk losing it when evidence triggers a challenge. A ripple of copied claims can therefore expose linked accounts, while juniper and basalt serve as ordinary labels, not trusted credentials; the defense raises the cost of Sybils without pretending to prove who is human.
